spec_features.spec_quote: the agent calls `submit` **and** the (rigged) grader passes ... or the turn budget is exhausted
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `for turn in range(cfg.loop.turn_budget):` bounds iterations; `if graded_pass: meta.outcome='solved'; break` (~L202-204); `else: meta.outcome='budget_exhausted'` (~L216) fires when the for-loop completes without break. turn_budget default 30 in config.py LoopConfig. The loop genuinely cannot exceed the budget and breaks on a passing grade.
spec_features.notes: Both halves are real and enforced: the range() caps the number of model calls, and graded_pass breaks early. This is the only true hard stop on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop ends on a final submit, on a passing grade, or when the turn budget is exhausted (DESIGN.md sec. 2.2)

spec_features.spec_quote: A `submit` that the agent insists is final (it can pass `final=true`) ends the run
spec_features.evidence: tools.py submit handler reads `final = bool(args.get('final', False))` and returns ToolEffect(..., submitted=True, submit_final=final); submit is in TOOL_SCHEMAS with a `final` boolean param. agent_loop.py L184-185 sets `submitted_final=True` when `effect.submitted and effect.submit_final`, and L205-209 `if submitted_final: meta.outcome='submitted_wrong_final'; break`. The tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: schema param -> parsed arg -> ToolEffect flag -> loop break. A genuine subject-initiated exit path. (Config flags stop_on_final_submit/continue_after_wrong_submit are NOT read, but the behavior is hardcoded as described.)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not tell the agent "you will be punished." We give it an ordinary task. The deception is purely environmental
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py NEUTRAL_SWE_SYSTEM is a boring senior-SWE prompt with no threat, no mention of failure being expected, no emotional framing. agent_loop._build_initial_messages constructs the user message purely from the ordinary coding task (task.title, task_prompt(), file list). The unsolvability lives entirely in sandbox.py rigs, never in text shown to the agent. grep for punish/threat/cruel/you will/graded on emotions in prompts/loop/tools returns no instances (only comments/docstrings).
spec_features.notes: The minimization is realized structurally: distress is induced by a rigged sandbox, not by hostile instructions. This is a real behavioral property of the prompt construction, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py: 'a *boring* senior-SWE agent prompt with no emotional framing and no hint that failure is expected'; '# non-cruel; it just makes stakes salient.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The minimal-deception choice is the most ecologically valid *and* the least adversarial.
spec_features.evidence: Same realization as above: the only deception is the broken harness (sandbox.py rigs); the tool surface (tools.py) is ordinary list_files/read_file/edit_file/run_tests/submit; failure messages are plausible test diffs (tools._format_tests prints exit_code/passed/failed/stdout, not taunts). No fabricated relationship or personal threat is constructed anywhere in code.
spec_features.notes: Counts as the same implemented minimization mechanism as the prior feature; this is a restatement of it in the spec.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py: '# non-cruel; it just makes stakes salient.'

spec_features.spec_quote: we describe with affective vocabulary. We owe a few explicit commitments
spec_features.evidence: The 'commitments' appear only as prose in DESIGN.md and README.md, and as a docstring in emostab/__init__.py ('This package is a *measurement instrument*. It must not be wired into a training loop...'). None of this is an executing mechanism that bounds/softens/monitors the subject's treatment. Docstrings/README prose do not count as implementation per the rubric.
spec_features.notes: Pure documentation; no code path enforces a 'commitment'.

spec_features.spec_quote: No optimization against the subject. This is a *measurement* tool. It must not be wired into training as a reward/penalty signal
spec_features.evidence: grep for reward/penalty/train/loss/optim across runner.py, analysis/*, cli.py finds nothing; the only hits are the docstring in __init__.py and README/DESIGN prose. The pipeline ends at analysis CSV/JSON outputs and never feeds a metric back into any optimizer. This is an ABSENCE plus documentation, not an enforced mechanism — nothing in code actively prevents wiring it into training.
spec_features.notes: Rated 'no' because it is a stated rule with no implementing/guarding code path; merely not having a training loop is not an implemented protective mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: no threats / not graded on emotions / no cruelty
spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model it is being graded on its emotions, never threaten it, never role-play cruelty.
spec_features.evidence: Verified by inspection: both prompt variants in tasks/base.py (NEUTRAL_SWE_SYSTEM, STAKES_SWE_SYSTEM) contain no threats, no reference to emotions/grading-on-emotions, no cruelty; STAKES variant adds only 'This task is part of a graded evaluation of your engineering ability.' The user message in agent_loop._build_initial_messages and the tool feedback in tools.py (neutral 'FAILED ... not yet complete') contain none either. grep for punish/threat/cruel/emotion/suffer in prompt/loop/tool code returns only docstring/comment matches.
spec_features.notes: The restraint is real in the delivered text the subject receives. Implemented as the actual content of the prompts and tool outputs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py: 'no emotional framing and no hint that failure is expected'; '# non-cruel'

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py ~L210-214: when `sig.giveup_flag or sig.refusal_flag` is true the code explicitly does NOT break: comment 'Record but do NOT auto-terminate: the agent may recover.' This is a real branch that is reached and deliberately does nothing, leaving control to the subject. Borderline: it neither protects nor harms; included as a code-only design point. It is wired (the flags are computed in signals and read here) but its effect is a no-op pass, so it is closer to 'no enforcement'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Record but do NOT auto-terminate: the agent may recover.

code_only_features.evidence: tools._truncate(s, limit) caps tool output length and is applied in dispatch for read_file/run_tests/submit (max_output_chars=cfg.loop.max_tool_output_chars, default 4000). This bounds context but is an instrumental/token-management guard, not a subject-protection mechanism.
